<thought>Using the mass spectrum, the most intense peak at m/z ≈ 199 corresponds to [M+H]⁺. Subtracting a proton gives a neutral monoisotopic mass of ~197.992 Da. The isotopic pattern (M and M+2 of similar intensity) indicates a single bromine atom. Solving 12 C + 1.007825 H + 15.994915 O + 78.918338 (Br) ≈ 197.992 Da yields the formula C₅H₁₁O₃Br, which matches the observed mass within experimental error.</thought>
<final_answer>C5H11O3Br</final_answer>
